findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context
findings.body: The timeout context is derived from the incoming request context, which is normally canceled when the handler returns. Since the legacy operation runs after the method returns, it can receive an already-canceled context and abort instead of writing. The same pattern is used for update, delete, and delete-collection, so mode 3 can leave legacy storage stale despite successful unified writes.

findings.title: Delete metric uses the resource name as the kind label
findings.body: This call passes `name` where the other storage-duration calls pass `options.Kind`. If that argument is the metric's kind label, every distinct deleted object name creates a separate label value, causing unbounded Prometheus cardinality and making the metric inconsistent with other operations. Pass the resource kind instead.

findings.title: Legacy delete-collection duration is recorded as a storage operation
findings.body: This goroutine measures the legacy `DeleteCollection` call but records it with `recordStorageDuration`, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to unified storage and the legacy metrics omit this operation. Use the legacy duration recorder; otherwise monitoring cannot accurately show whether the asynchronous legacy write is succeeding or slowing down.
